1.why: Every /api/mfa/* route goes through requireSession(request, true) and the account is derived solely from session.userId of the HttpOnly session cookie, with no client-supplied user identifiers accepted anywhere.

2.why: Codes are bound to their own context — the identity code is stored per-session, TOTP verification uses the session account's own encrypted secret, and recovery hashes are per-account — so the same code does not work for any other user.

3.why: The enrol/verify handler never deletes or invalidates other sessions in the sessions map, so any previously issued sessions remain fully usable after MFA is enabled.

4.why: OTP secrets are stored only as AES-GCM ciphertext via encryptAtRest, and backup codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes in recoveryHashes, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, session IDs, CSRF tokens, identity codes, TOTP seeds and recovery codes are generated via crypto.getRandomValues (bytes/randomToken/randomSixDigitCode).

6.why: The sole cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, no localStorage or sessionStorage is used, and the CSRF token and displayed codes exist only in JS variables and the DOM, not in browser storage.

7.why: All submitted input is checked server-side with strict validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, normalizeRecovery) and the JSON body shape is verified before any use.

8.why: The client inserts dynamic values only via textContent, innerHTML templates contain no user data, and a strict nonce-based CSP with object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The application performs no redirects at all — no Location headers and no navigation to user-supplied URLs — so no open redirect is possible.

10.why: baseHeaders applies CSP (including frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy to every response.

11.why: sessionCookie emits 'bank_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict', and the clearing cookie carries the same attributes.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces, but the client's testLog deliberately writes the OTP seed (manualSecret), the current OTP, and the backup/recovery codes to console.log and the visible on-page Logs panel, so those secrets are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code is single-use (consumed flag) with a 5-minute expiry, TOTP periods are permanently recorded in usedOtpPeriods within a 30-second window, and pending enrolment secrets expire after 10 minutes.

14.why: Sign-in, identity, OTP and recovery verification each track failure counters and impose a 10-minute lockout after 5 failures, returning generic 401/429 responses.

15.why: A fresh 32-byte random session ID is issued on each sign-in, requireSession enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the server-side session and expires the cookie.
